title: POC weekly sync - quantization INT8/FP8 results review
summary: Weekly sync to review INT8 vs FP8 quantization experiments on the recommendation model, performance deltas, quality impact, and next tuning steps. Agreement to run token-level evals and a 24h stability run on Dedicated nodes. SE to share updated benchmark sheet and config diffs.

Customer to run token-level evals on 3k prompts and share failures (Samir) - by 2026-09-14
Schedule 24h stability run on Dedicated - tentative start 2026-09-15 (Lena/Jess)

transcription:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-09-08 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Aurelia Head of ML), Jess Nguyen (Aurelia SRE), Elena Morris (Aurelia CTO), Tom Baker (Data Eng)

Auto-summary: Quick pulse on the INT8/FP8 experiments on the rec model. INT8 gave ~2.3x memory reduction and ~1.2x throughput; FP8 showed slightly better quality on long-context prompts but with marginal extra memory. Agreed to run more token-level evals, share full logs, and schedule longer stability run on Dedicated.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — results from the quant runs, perf deltas, any regressions, and next steps. Marco, you wanna kick off with the numbers?
[00:24] Marco: Yeah, sure. so we ran two main branches, INT8 path and the FP8 path, both on the same model snapshot — the 13b rec variant. note: there was a small change in the kv cache handling so please see the diff. INT8 reduced model memory from about 24g to 9.8g, so ~2.4x, and tokens per second improved by ~20% for short queries.
[00:58] Samir: Wait, 2.4x memory? that seems high, is that with activation quant or just weights?
[01:08] Marco: mostly weights + some activation folding. there's a little bit of custom kernel selection in the runtime; might read as K-V cash in the raw logs, sorry the auto-transcript sometimes says K-V cash.
[01:22] Jess: how about latency tail? p95/p99?
[01:27] Marco: good call — p95 improved by about 12% on INT8, p99 was basically flat, maybe 3% worse in some burst cases because of extra dequant overhead for long sequences. FP8 had a slightly better p99 — we saw p99 drop by 8% vs baseline, but FP8 used more memory (around 14g) so capacity-wise it's between baseline and INT8.
[01:57] Elena: qualitatively, any hallucination uplift or BLEU-like metric drop? we have some sensitive downstream checks.
[02:05] Priya: we ran the standard 2k prompt eval set plus a 400 long-context subset. FP8 preserved long-context coherence better, fewer truncation artefacts on the +2k tokens, INT8 had a few regressions on entity linking cases.
[02:28] Samir: can you quantify the regressions? like top-k accuracy drop?
[02:33] Marco: on the entity linking microtask, INT8 lost ~1.8 percentage points, FP8 lost ~0.4 points. on the general recommendation ranking metric we saw <0.5% change for INT8 and negligible for FP8.
[02:51] Tom: those entity linking drops are concerning for our use case. is there a middle ground?
[02:58] Marco: yeah there's a hybrid route — keep critical layers in fp16 and quantize the rest to int8; we tested a 2-layer fp16 prefix and that got the entity linking loss under 0.6 points while keeping memory ~1.7x reduced.
[03:18] Samir: interesting, is that easy to automate in your rollout? we don't want to change a bunch of ops for production.
[03:24] Lena: we can provide a rollout config: canary with fallback to fp16 baseline, or step upgrades with exact layer masks. Redwood Dedicated makes it easy to pin versions and auto-fallback.
[03:36] Jess: for Dedicated what's the expected throughput? if we go INT8 hybrid, can we reclaim nodes?
[03:42] Marco: yes. with INT8 pure you could pack ~2.2x more replicas per GPU - that was on the A100 family. with a hybrid it's about ~1.6x. exact depends on sequence length distribution; your workload avg seq is 220 tokens.
[03:59] Elena: what about regulatory concerns — encryption and logs? since we'll be on Dedicated, we need KMS integration and audit logs for the stability run.
[04:07] Lena: yes, Private/Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS; we can enable node-level audit logs and SSO access. we'll share the security pack after the call.
[04:18] Samir: please, also include a note on deterministic outputs — quant can be non-deterministic with fused kernels. we had a bug before where we saw small RNG diffs on fp8 kernels.
[04:30] Priya: noted. we have deterministic mode in the runtime; FP8 fused kernels currently have a known non-determinism edge case — need to toggle a slower path for exact reproducibility.
[04:41] Samir: ok. next, the quality checks — Marco you mentioned token-level evals?
[04:46] Marco: yes we pushed token-level diffs to the benchmark sheet (link shared). key thing: INT8 shows token-level mismatch concentrated in rare tokens and named entities, FP8 mismatches are distributed but lower overall magnitude.
[05:02] Tom: can you share failure examples now?
[05:05] Marco: I pasted a sample into the sheet and in the shared drive: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/aurelia-quant — take a look.
[05:14] Samir: thanks. real question — if we see business-impacting fails, what's the rollback plan?
[05:19] Lena: canary + auto-fallback. Redwood can route a percent of traffic to the new quantized variant and automatically roll back based on your quality thresholds (we can tie to token-level regression alerts).
[05:31] Jess: latency under load — did you test concurrency spikes?
[05:34] Marco: we did a simulated burst test; INT8 had more variance in the dequant path which caused occasional p99 spikes under extreme burst; FP8 was smoother but heavier. we recommend a small burst buffer and ramping policy for canary.
[05:50] Elena: any mention of competitor solutions? are they doing similar quantization?
[05:55] Marco: others like Vertex have quant libs but less end-to-end control and you usually have to stitch the runtime yourself; Redwood's advantage is the integrated runtime + rollout.
[06:06] Samir: ok. about the Dedicated test — what exact configs do you need from our side?
[06:11] Lena: we'll need the model artifact tag, a small config override file (we'll template it), and access to the token-level eval set. Jess will provision a dedicated test pool or we can run on Redwood Dedicated with a VPC peering.
[06:25] Jess: provisioning note — we can spin up a 2-GPU test bed but need the timeline.
[06:29] Lena: target 24h stability run starting 2026-09-15, subject to your provisioning.
[06:35] Samir: sounds good. next, any perf tuning knobs you tried?
[06:39] Marco: we tuned batch sizing and kernel selection; dynamic batching helped CAPEX, but for low-latency path we recommend smaller batches and sticky sessions with KV cache kept live. Also prefetching the kv cache for known-heavy routes helped reduce p99 by ~6%.
[06:59] Tom: sticky sessions — that requires affinity, is that supported on your routing?
[07:03] Priya: yes we support request routing with affinity keys; it's in the rollout config.
[07:10] Samir: can you summarize the recommendation again — best option if we prioritize cost, and if prioritize quality?
[07:15] Marco: cost-first: pure INT8 with monitoring and token-level thresholds; quality-first: FP8 or hybrid where top 4 layers remain fp16; balanced: hybrid with two fp16 prefix layers — that gives ~1.7x memory savings and <0.6pp quality hit.
[07:33] Elena: what about inference engine compatibility — any changes to our client?
[07:37] Lena: no API changes, same Redwood endpoints. only model variant tag changes, and the rollout config.
[07:42] Jess: nice. about the 24h run, what metrics will you collect?
[07:46] Marco: we'll collect token throughput, latency quantiles, memory usage, token-level diffs, per-prompt quality scores, and error rates. logs will be in the benchmark sheet with raw traces.
[07:58] Samir: can you also add prompt families tags so we can slice by verticals?
[08:01] Marco: yes — we added tags in the sheet, please review.
[08:06] Tom: are there any known FP8 kernel bugs we should be aware of?
[08:10] Priya: the main one is an edge-case with very long sequences and mixed attention types — we have a workaround to force a slower but stable kernel. we'll include that in the config.
[08:21] Elena: ok this is helpful. let's talk about success criteria for the pilot — Samir?
[08:26] Samir: for us success is: 1) <=0.5pp drop on business-critical metrics (recall/top-k), 2) >1.5x reduction in compute unit cost, 3) stable p99 within 10% of baseline.
[08:38] Lena: good measurable goals. we'll align the canary thresholds to those.
[08:42] Jess: for the rollout, can we run a 5% traffic canary for 48h then 25% for 24h?
[08:49] Lena: yep that's the normal cadence; we'll also add automatic rollback triggers.
[08:53] Samir: anything else from Redwood?
[08:55] Marco: I'll attach the raw logs and the kernel selection diff; also the exact step we used to force hybrid layers.
[09:03] Elena: sounds good. small nit: can you mark the entity linking prompts so we can review?
[09:07] Marco: done, they're in the sheet under the "entity_linking" tag.
[09:11] Tom: and the sample failure cases?
[09:12] Marco: pasted.
[09:14] Lena: ok next steps recap — Marco will send updated sheet and config diffs, Samir will run token-level eval, Jess will provision Dedicated test bed, and we'll aim to start the 24h run on 9/15.
[09:28] Samir: quick question — any recommended quant libs we should try in-house?
[09:33] Marco: if you want to run locally, we recommend our open quant kit or Intel's QAT for x86, but you will miss the runtime kernel optimizations Redwood provides; we can share a small docker for reproducibility.
[09:46] Priya: also note, if you move to Private deployment later we'll provide the same runtime so no additional changes.
[09:54] Lena: cool. I'll send the security pack, benchmark link, and a template for the config override.
[09:59] Elena: thanks. any blockers?
[10:02] Jess: provisioning timeline is the only one; otherwise good.
[10:06] Lena: great, thanks all. we'll follow up in the sheet and set up the 24h job once provisioned.
[10:12] Meeting ended.

References/Artifacts shared: Benchmark sheet & sample failures: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/aurelia-quant; Security pack (sent after call); Kernel diff patch: sent to shared drive.
